answers.reason: The statement leaves out that the notice must describe the change fully. It also gets the exception wrong: it calls the § 201.26 exception a 'labeling' exception, which the text does not say, and treats it as a full exemption, but (a)(1)(ii) still requires a granted exception to be reported in the annual report.

The quote is exact and both triggers in (c)(5)(i)-(ii) are covered. But the statement drops the limit in (c)(5)(ii) that, when information is missing, distribution is barred only until the supplement is amended to supply it, so the prohibition reads as open-ended.
